questions.cardText:
[Cultural Studies] Which Hindu deity is honored during the Holi festival?
A. Ganesha
B. Brahma
C. Krishna
Answer: C. According to one version of the myth, the blue-skinned Krishna playfully colored the face of his beloved Radha to make her look more like him. This act is believed to be the origin of throwing colored powder during the festival.
questions.de: Welche dunkelhäutige hinduistische Gottheit soll durch das spielerische Färben mit ihrer geliebten Radha den Ursprung des Farbpulverwerfens an Holi begründet haben?
questions.en: Which dark-skinned Hindu deity's playful colouring with his beloved Radha is said to be the origin of throwing coloured powder at Holi?

timeline.labelEn: King Harsha's Ratnavali mentions the festival of holikotsav (7th century)
timeline.labelDe: König Harshas „Ratnavali“ erwähnt das Fest „Holikotsav“ (7. Jahrhundert)

questions.notes: Wikipedia's version of the legend has Krishna, worried about his dark skin, letting Radha colour HIS face (the card has Krishna colouring Radha's); the question avoids the direction. Holi also honours the Prahlada/Holika legend (Vishnu as Narasimha), so the card's 'honored' is one of several associations.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following aquatic animals have been found to be capable of climbing trees?
A. Jellyfish
B. Seahorse
C. Fish
Answer: C. Some species of mudskippers can use their pectoral fins to “walk” on land and even climb trees.
questions.de: Welche amphibisch lebenden Grundeln bewegen sich mit ihren Brustflossen über Schlamm und klettern sogar auf tief hängende Äste?
questions.en: Which amphibious gobies use their pectoral fins to skip across mud and even climb low-hanging tree branches?

timeline.labelEn: Bloch and Schneider describe the mudskipper genus Periophthalmus
timeline.labelDe: Bloch und Schneider beschreiben die Schlammspringer-Gattung Periophthalmus

questions.notes: Card's answer is just 'Fish'; the explanation names mudskippers, which the open question asks. Timeline from the Periophthalmus article (authority Bloch & J. G. Schneider, 1801).
